subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram provider intermittently stalls despite stable direct Bot API connectivity

question: Should this Telegram SOCKS stall be owned as a shared scheme-aware proxy-helper fix, a Telegram force-IPv4/operator-policy mitigation, or both?
rationale: Both candidate PRs change compatibility-sensitive network behavior, and the current issue still lacks live current-release SOCKS proof that would make one path clearly sufficient.

options.title: Pursue Shared Proxy Repair
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84582 or a replacement to fix explicit and env proxy scheme handling with focused tests and live SOCKS proof.

options.title: Accept Force-IPv4 As Separate Mitigation
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78438 as an operator opt-in for broken IPv6 while keeping this SOCKS proxy bug open until proxy behavior is proven.

options.title: Wait For Reporter Diagnostics
options.body: Keep the issue open but defer code changes until a current-release service-context SOCKS reproduction narrows the root cause.

recommendation.title: Pursue Shared Proxy Repair
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84582 or a replacement to fix explicit and env proxy scheme handling with focused tests and live SOCKS proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily in Telegram transport behavior, with shared proxy input from steipete or jesse-merhi likely needed for the helper layer.
